satellite.tab.place.tooltip: Where the map lies on the Earth: find the place, put the map there, set it exactly
satellite.tab.pictures.tooltip: Pictures from the air: the source, loading them, how opaque they lie
satellite.tab.more.tooltip: Your own pictures, keys and tile servers, disk space
satellite.title: Satellite and terrain
satellite.search.placeholder: Find a place: a town, a street, an address
satellite.search.tooltip: Looks the place up with OpenStreetMap's Nominatim; Enter searches too
satellite.find.tooltip: Looks the place up with OpenStreetMap's Nominatim
satellite.world: This map has world coordinates ([worldcoordinates]): it lies on the Earth by itself, its tiles are Web Mercator tiles.
satellite.place_here.tooltip: Then click on the map of the world: the middle of the orange tile goes there
satellite.placing: Click on the map of the world...
satellite.at_middle.tooltip: Lays the orange tile's middle on the middle of the map of the world
satellite.rotation.tooltip: How far the map's north is turned from true north, clockwise
satellite.anchor.none: 1. Find the place.  2. Press "Place the map here" and click on the map of the world: the orange tile, the map's middle, goes there.
@satellite.anchor.set: {latitude} and {longitude} are decimal degrees written with a point, shown unchanged
satellite.reference.none: Place the map first; then the point that stays put while you turn and scale it can be chosen here.
@satellite.reference.set: {first} and {second} are distances written by satellite.direction
satellite.direction: {meters, number, 0.##} m {direction, select, east {east} west {west} north {north} other {south}}
@satellite.direction: {direction} is east, west, north or south and chooses the word: keep it in English
satellite.own.note: A scan, a screenshot, an old plan: laid on tiles and lined up by eye. No place on the Earth needed.
satellite.tile.sw: The tile at the picture's south-west corner
satellite.tile.ne: The tile at the picture's north-east corner
satellite.load_file: Load image file over these tiles...
satellite.load_file.tooltip: A JPEG, PNG, BMP or TGA picture stretched over these tiles; the copy stays in the project
satellite.picture.item: {file} ({count, plural, one {# tile} other {# tiles}} from {west}, {south})
satellite.fit.title: Line up {file}
satellite.turn_left.tooltip: Turns the picture a quarter anticlockwise
satellite.turn_right.tooltip: Turns the picture a quarter clockwise
satellite.turn.tooltip: Turned clockwise in degrees; drag the label or type a value
satellite.east.tooltip: Moved east in metres; drag the label or type a value
satellite.north.tooltip: Moved north in metres; drag the label or type a value
satellite.size.tooltip: Size against the tiles, 1 for stretched over them; drag the label or type a value
satellite.size_info: {width, number, 0.0} × {height, number, 0.0} m{hasPixel, select, yes {, {pixel, number, 0.00} m a pixel} other {}}
satellite.reset.tooltip: Stretched over its tiles again, unturned and unmirrored
satellite.remove.tooltip: Takes the picture off its tiles and out of the project
satellite.keys.note: Everything works without a key. With your own free key these may be sharper in some places; the key stays on this computer.
satellite.key.tooltip: Your key for {name}; it stays on this computer
satellite.own.name: Name
satellite.own.name.tooltip: How the server is called in the source list
satellite.own.url.tooltip: {zxy} are filled in; a WMS gets {bbox} (EPSG:3857) and {widthHeight}; {key} is your key
@satellite.own.url.tooltip: The values are placeholders of the URL, shown unchanged
satellite.own.attribution.tooltip: Shown under the map while its pictures show
satellite.own.zoom.tooltip: The finest zoom the server has
satellite.own.wms: WMS: each tile asked by its {bbox}
@satellite.own.wms: {bbox} is a placeholder of the URL, shown unchanged
satellite.own.url_note: {zxy} are filled in; a WMS gets {bbox} (EPSG:3857) and {widthHeight}; {key} is your key.
@satellite.own.url_note: The values are placeholders of the URL, shown unchanged
satellite.own.add.tooltip: Adds the server to the source list
@satellite.own.source: {wms} is yes or no and chooses a part: keep it in English
satellite.own.remove.tooltip: Takes the server out of the source list
satellite.copies.tooltip: Compressed copies of the full pictures that make zooming in smooth. They are kept on this computer, not in the project, up to the limit shown; the ones used longest ago go first. Deleting them is safe: they are made again when needed.
satellite.copies.clear.tooltip: Deletes the compressed copies; they are made again when a tile comes near the view
@satellite.usage: {used} and {cap} are sizes such as 120 MB
satellite.source.tooltip: Where the pictures come from; none of them needs a key. The sharpest is chosen at the map's middle. "OpenStreetMap map" draws the map as openstreetmap.org shows it, with streets' names, houses and stops, to build over by eye.
satellite.tile_picture.tooltip: How many pixels each tile's picture keeps. The map shows 1024 a tile and the full picture of the tiles in view when you zoom in.
satellite.with_heights.tooltip: Takes the ground's heights from the AWS terrain tiles too; the shaped ground of those tiles is replaced, in one step Ctrl+Z takes back
satellite.load_all.tooltip: Pictures (and heights) for every tile of the map
satellite.load_tile.tooltip: Pictures (and heights) for the tile selected in the map
satellite.load_tile.tooltip_none: Select a tile in the map first
satellite.heights_only.tooltip: Terrain heights for every tile, without pictures
satellite.auto: New tiles get pictures by themselves
satellite.auto.tooltip: A tile added to the map gets its picture from the air at once, and its terrain heights too when "Also load terrain heights" is ticked
satellite.cancel.tooltip: Stops loading; tiles done so far stay
satellite.edges.fit.tooltip: Their edge takes the loaded heights, fading out 60 m into the tile; Ctrl+Z takes it back
satellite.edges.leave.tooltip: Keeps the step at their edge
satellite.edges.stepped: {tiles, plural, one {# tile beside the loaded heights was not loaded: the ground steps at its edge.} other {# tiles beside the loaded heights were not loaded: the ground steps at their edge.}}
satellite.relative: Relative: the middle tile's mean height is 0 m
satellite.relative.tooltip: Takes the middle tile's mean height off all heights, as most OMSI maps lie near 0 m; off keeps the height above the sea
satellite.smoothing.tooltip: How far each height is smoothed with its neighbours; 0 for none
satellite.base.measured: Measured at the middle tile on the first load.
satellite.measure.tooltip: The next load measures the middle tile's mean height again; tiles loaded before may then step at their edges
satellite.terrain_note: Terrain: Mapzen Terrain Tiles on AWS Open Data (SRTM, USGS 3DEP, GMTED2010, ETOPO1, Copernicus EU-DEM and others).
satellite.opacity.tooltip: How opaque the pictures lie on the ground
satellite.overlay_note: The pictures stay in the project and are not exported. Check a source's terms before you share pictures made from it.
satellite.exact.fold: Exact place: reference point, scale, moving
satellite.exact.note: The reference point stays where it is while the map is turned and scaled. Pick a crossing of the map, then paste where it lies on the Earth (on a web map: right click, copy the coordinates).
satellite.pick.tooltip: Then click the map: that point becomes the reference point and stays where it is on the Earth
satellite.middle_of_tile.tooltip: Makes the middle of the reference point's tile the reference point
satellite.lies_at.tooltip: Latitude and longitude, as web maps copy them: 52.5200, 13.4050. Enter or leaving the field moves the map there
satellite.scale.tooltip: Metres of ground one metre of the map covers: 1 for a map drawn true to scale, 1.2 if it is drawn 20 % too small
satellite.move.tooltip: How many metres a press moves the map on the Earth; the pictures follow at once
satellite.move.west.tooltip: Moves the map west on the Earth by the step
satellite.move.east.tooltip: Moves the map east on the Earth by the step
satellite.move.north.tooltip: Moves the map north on the Earth by the step
satellite.move.south.tooltip: Moves the map south on the Earth by the step
satellite.fit.note: Pick two crossings in the map and paste where each lies on the Earth: the map is moved, turned and, if ticked, scaled to meet both.
satellite.fit.pick.tooltip: Then click the map: the point in the map to fit
satellite.fit.lies_at.tooltip: Latitude and longitude of this point on the Earth: 52.5200, 13.4050
satellite.fit.scale.tooltip: Also takes the scale from the distance between the two points; without it the map keeps its scale
satellite.fit.button.tooltip: Moves and turns the map so that both points meet their positions
